fit-focused-dressing-for-body-type-shoul.summary: Choosing garment cuts and fit that broaden the shoulders and narrow the waist so your torso reads as a V-taper.

quick.overview:
Fit-focused dressing means picking cuts and tailoring that emphasise wide shoulders and a narrower waist, so your torso reads as a V-taper the moment you put the clothes on.

Fit and tailoring change where garments sit and how much volume they add, which shifts the apparent shoulder-to-waist proportion. Body-shape literature links wide shoulders and a lower waist-to-chest ratio in men with perceived attractiveness; no trial has tested specific clothing cuts for this.
quick.how: People look for structured shoulders, jackets and shirts that follow the waist rather than hang boxy, and tailoring that takes in extra fabric at the midsection. It is often paired with training that builds the shoulders and back. The effect shows as soon as the clothes are worn.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented for ordinary clothing choices. Off-the-rack sizing varies, and tailoring adds cost.

angle.text: Garment cuts that broaden the shoulders and take in the waist make your torso read as a V-taper as soon as you wear them. The change is visible on the spot, and wide shoulders with a narrow waist are linked in the body-shape literature to perceived attractiveness.

vertical-stripes-monochrome-elongation.summary: Dressing in vertical stripes or a single colour to look taller and slimmer, a long-running piece of style advice.

quick.overview:
The idea is that vertical stripes and head-to-toe single-colour outfits create an unbroken line that makes you look taller and slimmer.

It draws on optical illusions such as the vertical-horizontal and Helmholtz illusions, where line direction and filled space change perceived length and width. Two i-Perception studies (2011 and 2013) reported that horizontal stripes looked narrower than vertical ones, with the effect varying between viewers; no study on monochrome outfits was found.
quick.how: People wear one colour or tonal shades from top to bottom, or choose garments with vertical pinstripes or seams, often combined with well-fitted tailoring. The look is seen as soon as the outfit is on.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented. How the effect reads varies between viewers.

angle.text: Vertical stripes and single-colour outfits are used to give an unbroken line that makes you look taller and slimmer. Perception studies of stripe direction have found mixed results, with some reporting horizontal stripes looking narrower.

photo-angle-maxxing.summary: Finding the camera angle, distance, lens and head tilt that make you look best in photos.

quick.overview:
Photo angle maxxing is working out which camera angle, distance, lens and head tilt give the most flattering pictures of you, so the same face looks better in the frame.

Perspective depends mainly on camera-to-subject distance. Close shots with wide-angle lenses enlarge nearby features such as the nose, while shooting from farther away with a longer focal length reduces those size differences. Portrait guides commonly cite roughly 75-135 mm (35 mm equivalent) for head shots.
quick.how: People take test shots from different heights, distances and tilts, compare them, and keep the settings that work. Many step back and use a longer lens or the zoom setting. The result is visible immediately.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented. The main downside is that photos can diverge from how you look in person.

angle.text: Testing camera angle, subject distance, lens and head tilt lets you find the framing where you photograph best. The change shows in the image right away, and the lens-distance physics behind it is well documented.

camera-lens-distortion-portrait-lens-85m.summary: Shooting with a longer portrait lens from farther back so your nose and face look more proportionate.

quick.overview:
Using a longer portrait lens, often 85-135 mm, from farther back keeps your nose and face looking more proportionate in photos.

Perspective distortion makes features nearest the lens look larger: a close wide-angle shot makes the nose look bigger relative to the face and shrinks the ears, while a longer lens from a greater distance flattens the effect. Photography references describe this optics well.
quick.how: People switch from a phone's wide lens to its portrait or zoomed setting, or use a camera with a medium telephoto lens, and stand a few metres back while still framing the face. It works on the day of the shoot.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented. A longer lens needs more space and may flatten depth in the picture.

angle.text: Shooting with a longer portrait lens from farther back makes the features closest to the camera, especially the nose, look less enlarged. The effect is visible in the photo itself and follows well-documented optics.

photo-lighting-golden-hour.summary: Shooting in soft, low-angle light such as golden hour so your face shows gentler shadows and lower contrast.

quick.overview:
Golden hour is the soft, warm light near sunrise and sunset. Shooting then, or in similarly soft light, gives your face lower contrast and gentler shadows in photos.

Low sun passes through more atmosphere, so the light is redder and more diffuse. Wikipedia notes it is often preferred for portraits because shadows are less dark and highlights are less likely to blow out.
quick.how: People schedule outdoor shots shortly after sunrise or before sunset, or use window light and open shade at other times, facing the light source. The difference is visible in the photo straight away.
quick.risks: No health risks. Golden hour is brief and depends on weather and location.

angle.text: Soft, low-angle light such as golden hour lowers contrast and softens shadows, giving a smoother-looking face in photos. The difference is visible in the shot itself and the physics of the light is clear.

dating-profile-photo-optimization.summary: Choosing and ordering dating-app photos using ratings from strangers so your profile shows your best shots.

quick.overview:
This is picking, editing and ordering your dating-app photos using outside feedback rather than your own preference, so the strongest shots lead your profile.

It is most often done with Photofeeler, where anonymous voters rate photos on attractiveness, trustworthiness and smartness. Supporters say outside ratings show how strangers see a photo, since friends and family may be overly kind. Forum members report mixed results, including top-rated photos that did not do best on apps.
quick.how: People upload candidate photos to a rating site, compare scores and comments, then choose and order the best ones for their profile. Results come back within hours to a day or so.
quick.risks: Low physical risk. Reported drawbacks include raters favouring smiling expressions, discouraging scores, and sharing photos with strangers.

angle.text: Rating candidate photos with anonymous voters lets you select and order the shots that come across best on a dating profile. Users value the outside view, though forum members report that top-rated photos do not always perform best on apps.

photofeeler-testing.summary: Uploading photos to be rated by anonymous voters on attractiveness, trustworthiness and smartness, used as a looks scoreboard.

quick.overview:
Photofeeler is a website where anonymous voters rate your photo, giving you numerical scores and comments on how strangers perceive you. Looksmaxxing forums use the scores as an informal gauge of looks and of which photo to post.

In dating tests, voters score attractiveness, trustworthiness and smartness; business and social tests use other traits. The company has published its own analyses and a 2019 paper by its staff on a neural network trained on its data.
quick.how: Users upload a photo into a business, social or dating test, receive scores and anonymous comments, and swap in new photos to compare. Voters earn credits by rating other people's photos.
quick.risks: Low physical risk. Forum members report scores that feel discouraging or biased toward smiles, and some report results that did not match dating-app performance. Photos are shown to strangers.

angle.text: Uploading a photo shows how anonymous voters score attractiveness, trustworthiness and smartness, which guides which pictures you use. Members disagree on how well the scores track real-world results, and the company's own analyses are the published evidence.

glasses-frame-selection-by-face-shape.summary: Choosing glasses frames to balance your face shape and flatter your features.

quick.overview:
This is choosing frame shapes that balance or complement your face, sometimes to add a more angular look or a hunter-eyes impression.

Frame lines, colour and size are said to contrast or echo your features and shift where the eye is drawn. Pairing rules by face shape are widely repeated in styling advice; no studies testing them were found.
quick.how: People try several shapes in a shop or with virtual try-on, comparing frames with their jaw, brow and cheekbone lines, and often ask for opinions or photos. The frames change the look as soon as they are worn.
quick.risks: No health risks. Poorly fitting frames can be uncomfortable, and the effect on appearance is subjective.

angle.text: Choosing frame shapes that balance or complement your face changes how your features read once the glasses are on, and some users aim for a hunter-eyes look. The pairing rules are widely repeated styling advice rather than tested findings.

glasses-to-mask-facial-flaws.summary: Wearing thick or large frames to draw attention away from eye bags, asymmetry or a prominent nose.

quick.overview:
Thick or oversized frames are worn to pull attention away from features people dislike, such as under-eye bags, asymmetry or the nose.

Frames add visual weight around the eyes and nose bridge, which proponents say redirects the viewer's attention to the eyewear. Glasses are now widely worn as fashion accessories, including non-prescription pairs.
quick.how: People pick bold acetate or oversized frames, sometimes non-prescription, and wear them daily or for photos. The effect is visible as soon as they are on.
quick.risks: No health risks. Results depend on the person, and heavy frames can feel uncomfortable on the nose or ears.

angle.text: Chunky or oversized frames add visual weight around the eyes, drawing attention away from bags, asymmetry or the nose. The frames are visibly present and change what stands out on the face.

colored-lenses-blue-light-glasses.summary: Tinted or blue-filtering lenses worn at screens for eye strain and, in some circles, fresher, less puffy-looking eyes.

quick.overview:
These are tinted or blue-filtering lenses worn at screens, marketed for eye strain and, in some looksmaxxing circles, for less puffiness around the eyes.

Coatings or tints absorb part of the blue end of the light spectrum, and yellow tints may shift colour slightly. Wikipedia reports that the American Academy of Ophthalmology does not recommend special eyewear for computer use and that the UK College of Optometrists says evidence does not support blue-blocking lenses for the general population. No studies on eye puffiness were found.
quick.how: People wear them during long screen sessions, often in the evening, as clear-looking coated lenses or with a visible yellow tint. Some add them to sleep and screen-time routines.
quick.risks: Low physical risk. Strongly tinted lenses can distort colour, and eye-care bodies do not recommend them for general use.

angle.text: Blue-light and tinted glasses are worn at screens for eye strain and, in some looksmaxxing circles, to keep the eye area looking fresher and less puffy. The puffiness link is anecdotal, and eye-care bodies cited by Wikipedia do not recommend them for strain.

skin-tone-matching-foundation-bb-cream-f.summary: Light foundation or BB cream matched to your skin to even out tone and cover redness and marks.

quick.overview:
A light foundation or BB cream matched to your skin evens out tone and covers redness, acne marks and blemishes, giving a clearer-looking complexion while worn.

Foundation is a long-established cosmetic category. BB cream is a lighter hybrid meant to combine coverage, moisturizer and sun protection in one step; it was developed for daily use by South Korean companies in the 1980s, and some brands market it to men. A well-matched shade is described as hard to detect.
quick.how: Men typically dab a small amount on the face with fingers or a sponge, focusing on red or uneven areas, and blend it into the neck. Colour matching in daylight matters, and results are seen immediately.
quick.risks: Low risk. Products can clog pores or irritate sensitive skin, and a mismatched shade looks visible, as shade ranges vary between brands.

angle.text: A light foundation or BB cream matched to your skin evens out tone and hides redness and marks, so your complexion looks clearer while it is worn. A well-matched shade is described as hard to detect.

men-s-makeup-contour-bronzer-highlight.summary: Subtle contour, bronzer and highlighter to make the jaw, cheekbones and nose look more defined.

quick.overview:
Subtle contour, highlighter and bronzer make the jaw, cheekbones and nose look more defined, so the face looks sharper while the makeup is worn.

Contouring uses a shade one or two tones darker than the skin in hollows and along edges to create shadow, while highlighting uses lighter shades on prominent areas. It has roots in theatrical makeup, was popularised by a 2000 book, and went mainstream on social media in the 2010s.
quick.how: People apply a darker shade under the cheekbones and along the jawline, a lighter one on the high points, and blend until the edges disappear. Men usually keep it light so it reads as natural, and the effect is immediate.
quick.risks: Low risk. Makeup can irritate or break out sensitive skin, and heavy or poorly blended application is easy to spot.

angle.text: Darker shades in the hollows and lighter ones on prominent edges create shadow and light that make the jaw, cheekbones and nose look more defined. The effect is visible while worn and follows standard makeup practice.

lip-balm-tinted-lip-color.summary: Wax-based lip balm, sometimes tinted, for smoother, healthier-looking lips with a natural shade.

quick.overview:
Lip balm keeps lips smooth and less chapped, and tinted versions add a natural shade, so lips look healthier and more even after application.

It works by forming a wax-like barrier that holds in moisture. Common bases include beeswax, candelilla and carnauba wax, lanolin, paraffin and petrolatum, sometimes with sunscreen, flavouring or dyes. Appearance research specific to lip balm is limited, and some research on lip balms is industry-funded.
quick.how: People apply it through the day, especially in cold or dry weather and before sleep, and pick a tinted or SPF version for added colour or sun protection. Results are visible straight after application.
quick.risks: Low risk. Fragrances, flavourings and some ingredients can irritate or cause allergic reactions in some people.

angle.text: Lip balm, sometimes tinted, keeps lips smooth and adds a natural shade, so they look moisturized and more even right after application. Appearance research specific to lip balm is limited.

teeth-whitening-before-photos.summary: Timing strips, trays or in-office whitening before a photo shoot or event for a visibly brighter smile.

quick.overview:
Whitening shortly before photos or an event lightens your teeth for a brighter smile on the day.

Wikipedia reports that in-office treatment may lighten teeth by 2 to 7 shades, while strips, trays and whitening toothpastes typically produce 1 to 2 shades. Methods include dentist-applied peroxide gels, tray-based gels, strips and rinses.
quick.how: People start strips or trays a week or two ahead or book an in-office session a few days before the event, then keep up with whitening toothpaste. Part of the immediate change may reverse within days.
quick.risks: Tooth and gum sensitivity is common, and gum irritation can occur from gels. Part of the shade change can fade within days, and people with dental restorations or gum disease usually check with a dentist first.

angle.text: Peroxide whitening timed before a photo shoot or event lightens your teeth for a brighter smile in pictures. The shade change is visible on the day, though part of it can fade over a few days.

undercut-fade-with-textured-top.summary: A haircut with short faded sides and a longer styled top that gives a clean outline and a sharper face and jaw look.

quick.overview:
A short faded side and back with a longer, textured top gives a clean outline and volume on top, and a skin fade is said to make the face and jaw look sharper.

The undercut dates to early 20th-century working-class men, was mainstream in the 1920s and 1930s and revived in the early 2010s, with adopters such as David Beckham. It is frequently cited in men's grooming advice as a flattering cut for many face shapes; those claims come from stylists and forums, not studies.
quick.how: People ask a barber for a fade or tapered sides and keep length on top, then style it with matte clay or paste for texture. It needs a trim every few weeks to keep the fade sharp, and the new look shows straight away.
quick.risks: Low risk. Maintenance is frequent, and the look needs enough hair on top to style.

angle.text: Short faded sides with a longer styled top give a clean outline and volume, and a skin fade is said to make the face and jaw look sharper. The haircut change is visible immediately and the style is widely recommended for many face shapes.

buzz-cut-for-thinning-hair.summary: Clipping hair very short so thinning or receding areas are less noticeable.

quick.overview:
Clipping hair to a short, uniform length reduces the contrast between sparse and dense areas, so thinning or a receding hairline is less noticeable.

Wikipedia notes the buzz cut is popular among people with thinning or receding hairlines. Pattern hair loss affects roughly 30 to 50 percent of men by age 50 and is described as reducing body-image satisfaction. The cut changes how hair loss looks rather than treating it.
quick.how: People shave down with clippers to a guard length, then keep it up with regular clipping, often combined with a beard and sun protection for the scalp. Medical options such as minoxidil and finasteride are separate.
quick.risks: Low risk. The scalp gets more sun exposure, and the cut does not slow hair loss.

angle.text: Clipping thinning or receding hair very short reduces the contrast between sparse and dense areas, so the thinning shows less. The look is visible immediately, and research on how shaved and bald looks are perceived is mixed.

hair-length-for-face-shape-long-hair-max.summary: Matching hair length and shape to your face, or growing hair out, to frame the jaw and forehead.

quick.overview:
Matching hair length, shape and parting to your face, or growing hair longer under labels such as long hair maxxing, frames your features and makes the jaw and forehead look more balanced.

Proponents say length and volume change perceived width and jaw outline through visual framing. Encyclopedic sources say stylists weigh face and head shape, hair type and the wearer's desired image. No published study has tested specific lengths for rated attractiveness.
quick.how: People try a stylist's recommendation or grow hair out over months, adjusting layers, parting and volume to the face. Growing out takes time, and styling products help it hold shape.
quick.risks: Low risk overall. Dermatology guidance links tight braids, extensions and dreadlocks to traction alopecia, and bleaching or dyeing has been linked in some research to health risks.

angle.text: Matching hair length and shape to your face, or growing it out, frames your features and makes the jaw and forehead look more balanced. The change in outline is visible as the hair grows or is styled.

facial-hair-as-camouflage-weak-chin.summary: Growing or shaping a beard to add apparent projection to a recessed chin or weak jawline.

quick.overview:
A beard adds apparent projection and definition along the chin and jaw, so a recessed chin or weak jawline looks stronger once it fills in.

Facial hair adds visual volume and an edge to the lower face. Wikipedia reports that in evolutionary psychology accounts beards signal dominance partly by increasing the perceived size of the jaw, and that clean-shaven faces have been rated less dominant than bearded ones. No trial has tested beards as chin camouflage specifically.
quick.how: People grow a beard for several weeks and shape the neckline and cheek lines, often keeping more length at the chin to add projection. Trimming and shaping matter as much as growth.
quick.risks: Low risk. Beards do not change the underlying bone, and patchy growth limits the result. Surgical options such as genioplasty are separate procedures with their own risks.

angle.text: Growing a beard along the jaw and chin adds apparent projection, making a recessed chin or weak jawline look stronger once it fills in. General research links beards to perceived jaw size and dominance, though chin-specific camouflage has not been tested.

posture-awareness.summary: Noticing and correcting how you stand and sit so you look taller, more open and more present.

quick.overview:
Posture awareness means noticing and correcting slouching, rounded shoulders and a forward head, so you look taller, more open and more confident.

Keeping the head over the shoulders and the spine upright counters the head-forward posture of phone and desk use. Research on posture mostly covers back and neck pain and ergonomics, including a school trial of a back education programme and a 2024 study of a photographic method for making posture actionable.
quick.how: People use mirrors, side-on photos, reminders and feedback to check their stance, often alongside strengthening work for the back and core. The change in stance is visible while held, and habits build over weeks.
quick.risks: Low risk. Persistent pain or a visible spinal curve is a matter for a clinician.

angle.text: Keeping your head over your shoulders and your spine upright counters the forward-head posture of phone and desk use, so you look taller and more present. The change is visible while held, and posture research has focused on pain rather than attractiveness.

body-language-presence-training.summary: Practising open stance, steady eye contact and slower movement to come across as more confident.

quick.overview:
Training an open stance, steady eye contact and slower movement is meant to make you come across as more confident and commanding.

Wikipedia defines body language as nonverbal communication through posture, gestures, facial expressions, eye movement, touch and use of space. Power-posing research found a reliable effect on how people feel but not on hormones, and an unclear effect on behaviour. Gesture meanings also vary across cultures.
quick.how: People rehearse in front of a mirror or on video, work on pace, posture and eye contact in conversation, and combine it with grooming and posture work. Practice builds over weeks.
quick.risks: Low risk. Gestures and eye contact can be read differently across cultures.

angle.text: Open stance, steady eye contact and slower movement are practised to make you appear more confident and commanding, often alongside posture and grooming. Research supports increased felt confidence more than measured changes in how others judge the person.
